notes.title: The Exhibition
notes.content:
We have discovered a Virtual Reality exhibition.

Encoded in a non-physical plane, this exhibition was found by myself and a research team called Rockband 1. We have been working to recover its corridors and exhibits from void-space. We believe it is part of a Compendium of all known things and events. Check it out!

You can access it via the Main Menu of The Utility Room.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42727016/0dfc792a704773481d51e5f2d04bc1167cccf174.png[/img]
^ Photoscanned bag of dog poo stolen from reality in London on the 14/06/2024.

[h2][b]It features:[/b][/h2]

People who may or may not be really dead.

Poo.

Backwards lumps.

Three K-hole simulations.

A pit.

Some boxes.


[u]Contributers/Band Members
[/u]
[url=https://www.instagram.com/patricktimetravels/]Patrick Bradley[/url], [url=https://www.instagram.com/alliaindiag/]Allia Georges[/url], [url=https://www.instagram.com/sam_jriley/]Sam Riley[/url], [url=https://www.instagram.com/king.lumps/]Lionel Marsden[/url]

[h3]Other Additions:[/h3]

There are also quite a few minor updates made to The Utility Room which I think are great quality of life improvements and fixes but I didn't write them down so I've forgotten what they were. What I can remember: 

Added a Height Offset in the settings if you want to play seated.

Community art added to The Sculpture Park.

3 New Languages: Spanish, French and Japanese.

Overhauled the lighting on The Cathedral and The Overpass (again) + Improved lighting on The View, Graveyard and Bowl.

Touching a worker during The Bottom zaps you badly.

Removed controller reflections from the mirror.

Many bug fixes.

[b]Working on getting The Utility Room on another platform this month and then hope to continue on the next game in the works later this year after a long well earned break. Hope you are all doing well and looking after yourselves! x[/b]

notes.title: Update 1.5 - Anxiety Nothingness and the Logic-Machine
notes.content:
Howdy folks! Apologies on lateness. Went home for Christmas. Hope yous all had a decent one.

This update is called [b]Anxiety Nothingness and the Logic Machine[/b]. You know.., that feeling you get when you stand up too quickly. In my mind, the Maze chapter is Anxiety Nothingness and The Computer is the Logic Machine. Make of that what you will. They've seen the biggest upgrades this update alongside parts of The Reprimand - in particular the Chase sequence.

I felt The Utility Room lagged a bit in the caves at the start (where'd I get that idea from?). Not intentionally, the foundation is there and its conceptually intact - but the implementation meant that they weren't fully realised. I like to think The Computer is a very strange place in minds-eye but you wouldn't know it playing through it. I'm hoping more of it is there now (literally) and that you guys and gals will be able to connect with it a bit more.

Bin Man is much bigger - as he should be. I had to reduce his intended size when you first meet him originally because I thought his eyeball couldn't be too big. Well, it can be a bit bigger and in this update he's twice as big, eyeballs and all. I think it makes him much more intimidating and is better suited to the power he beholds. It also prevents him looking as goofy which was an unintended consequence of his downsizing. Not something you want for the caretaker of the known Universe. Or is it?

Here are the major changes:


[h1][b]Major Changes
[/b]
[/h1]
[b]- Updated to Unreal Engine 5.3

- The Computer has been re-designed.

- The first cave has been re-designed.

- The Maze has had an upgrade.

- Major performance boost across the game (Fixed Foveated Rendering)

- The Cathedral has had a minor redesign

- Some Changes to the Reprimand (Ending)

- Overhauled the Chase sequence.

- Bin Man is twice as big in The Meeting and The Reprimand.

- Added a First Person Mode (Experimental).[/b]

Hope you like the changes and additions!

notes.title: Update 1.4.9 - New hands, New Modes, and a New Bedroom
notes.content:
Hows about that Jacob Geller video?! I watched that leaning against a door with a hand on my heart and another covering my eyes. Big thanks to my housemates Patrick for accompanying me through that ordeal - aside from that, its the best thing thats ever happenned.

Its a shame "Who's Lila?" looked so good. Why couldn't he have picked a bad game to go alongside The Utility Room? Thats a joke of course. Anyway all of that aside the video opens things up for the next game which you should be able to wishlist today (If thats something you wanted to do).
It was meant to be a more marketable game but I think its going to be stranger than the last, or rather this one - not the same scope but definitely more experimental. We'll see. Anyways UPDATE 1.4.9 brings...

[b]INDEX USERS READ BOTTOM TEXT*[/b]

[h3]- NEW HANDS[/h3]
	yeah some people caught on that it was the default Unreal Engine hands with a rock texture. I snuck these in yesterday. It was only a problem for people who knew that but it was naughty on my behalf - I've switched them out with some weird skinny measly ones I think match the vibe better.
[h3]- NEW MODE[/h3]
	Casual Mode - this won't excite most of you but its a more ACCESSABLE and TELEPORT ONLY way of playing the game. Probably better for Seated Players as it doesn't have the jump and it skips THE MAZE level (the level that makes you want to blow your brains out). You can switch to it in the pause menu or choose it upon starting the game.
[h3]- BEDROOM DE-DECORATED[/h3]
	The bedroom during The Reprimand has been redecorated or rather de-decorated. I felt there was too much going on.

and... Deprecated SteamVR. Now entirely OpenXR (you shouldn't notice anything different. If you use SteamVR make it your default OpenXR runtime).

[i](Note: If you run into issues this update upon loading a map like being unable to jump you might have to delete your save in the Chapter Select. I've been making changes that affect how you navigate and things might have frankensteined between versions).[/i]

Other changes

- The Computer is slightly more explorable with some small areas opened up. 
- Scenic areas in The Computer are less enticing (darker, look unnavigable) so it should put players off thinking they can go off-piste. I've also added some extra rocks to disuade players.
- Added 2 more slugs.
- The Slug collectable has been added to The Computer if people can't find it in the Maze or are playing Casual.
- The Doors are closer together preventing you from teleporting through the gap in the middle.
- A bug report button has been added to the main menu.
- The slugs are less likely to move over small rocks in The Computer.
- More minicubes have been added to The Computer.
- Added a new tutorial screen upon arriving at The Utility Room for Casual Mode players.
- You can now switch between Casual/HMD oriented/Controller oriented movement in the pause menu.
- Controls in the pause menu has been renamed to "Controls/Settings".
- Added a 45 second delay that moves you on in the Bedroom during The Reprimand to prevent dawdling.

Bug Fixes
- Fixed a bug that causes you to fall upon seeing the intro text.
- Prevented a fall through the map on The Mouth and The Pendulum.
- Eased the sound on the Predator's cameo/jumpscare during The Mouth.
- Prevented the falling sound playing when switching versions.

Here's the fantastic Jacob Geller Video if you didn't see it:
[previewyoutube=ZDrHpmkL4rY;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]ALSO! PLEASE SEND ANY ARTWORK OR 3D MODELS YOU THINK RELATE TO OR ARE INSPIRED BY THE GAME AND ILL ADD THEM TO THE SCULPTURE PARK WITH A CREDIT. [/b]

Keep resolutions/file size low ~5mb and <25,000 polygons.

POST THEM ON THE SUBREDDIT/DISCORD and I'll reach out or send them to me directly at lionelpantonmarsden@gmail.com

notes.title: Update 1.4.8 - Changes to Smooth Locomotion
notes.content:
- Smooth locomotion is by default now controller-oriented. Previously it was HMD oriented because the player swinging their arms would cause them to move backwards in mid-air as their controller pitch/yaw changed. I managed to fix this by switching to HMD oriented only whilst the player is in the air.

- Stronger vibrations when the player executes the leap.

- I've added a Post-processing effect that makes the screen darker as the leap charges up.

- Added another step down at the end of The Computer.

- Added a hint that states "Use Teleport" during the Cathedral if players fail on the slip n slide 3 times. (In case they're using smooth locomotion and forget they have teleport also)

- Prevented climbing in the first 2 chapters. The inclusion of climbing is for FUN only (except for the Canyon level in the extended edition) but its inclusion was confusing players into thinking it was a primary gameplay element. I've turned it off in the first two chapters to disuade people and keep them to teleport and jump. 

[b]Hopefully this update will prevent people pointing a gun at their own face during The Maze as it was easy to walk off the edges when looking around with Head oriented smooth locomotion.

You also get to see yourself get crushed during The Run whilst still running to the other side.[/b]

notes.title: Update 1.4.5 - Index Optimisations and other changes
notes.content:
[i]finally got my hands on an Index. Blows my mind to think I had the hubris to release the game without testing it on the headset. Well.. I didn't have the funds, and I still don't but I've managed to blag one and I discovered the game isn't as playable in some aspects as it is on Quest Headsets so I've made some improvements. They are:[/i]

- The haptic vibrations for the jump have been vastly improved for Index Controllers and change on start up depending on your controllers.

- The View among other GPU intense areas have been optimised for the Index's extra FOV. I'd suggest playing on Medium.

- Better tutorial for teleporting at the start of the game.

- Areas across the game are brighter for the Index's darker displays.

- You can skip chapters with "S" on your keyboard if you get stuck. If you die on The Maze too many times it suggests this after giving you a hint.

- The Boulder's vista is now visible on Medium graphics settings.

- The trigger for Bin Man appearing is now easier to overlap.

- The game defaults to "Medium" quality settings for Index and "High" for Quest headsets.

notes.title: Improved Leap
notes.content:
Just left Venice Immersive yesterday. It was a pleasure to meet everyone there! Special thanks to Liz and Michel for hosting the event and for considering The Utility Room worthy of selection. Onto the next one!

[u][b]LEAP[/b][/u]

I've changed how the leap functions to make it more user friendly and satisfying. These changes are:

- The vibration now matches the beats of the leap sfx.
- The initial vibration is stronger creating a sense of the leap being engaged.
- A glitch wherein the leap sound played without haptics or functionality when the player tries consecutive leaps has been fixed.
- The vibrations are stronger and linear as it charges up making it clearer when the player should swing their arms.
- The sound has better spatialization on the controllers and now also plays in stereo.

Other changes

- The light fades on the floating platform in THE REPRIMAND when Bin Man appears which should dissuade players from moving backwards.
- Added some lights to the darker caves during The View so people don't think the caves are deeper than they appear.
- Better teleport tutorial when players arrive at the platform.

notes.title: Update 1.4
notes.content:
[i]I’m very excited to announce [b]The Utility Room[/b] has been invited to feature in the [b]Venice Immersive[/b] Best of section, at the 80th Mostra Internazionale
d'Arte Cinematografica (80th Venice International Film Festival). 

I’ve made a few changes to the project in anticipation of its display on the Venice Immersive Island (Isola del Lazzaretto Vecchio) that I’ve now also made to the Steam build. Here they are! They are mostly regarding sound and music but there have also been some changes to the 2 playable modes and some of the environments.[/i]

[b][u]Main[/u][/b]

[b]New Track[/b]: The Finale of the Reprimand now has new music more befitting of the climax. I felt the last one was too cosmic and corny. Big props to the games composer Nicky Vella for sorting that out.

[b]The Chase Redesign[/b]: The sequence in the reprimand where Binman chases you around his brutalist lightning-storm hellscape has been redesigned with glitchy rocks, glitchy sound and a glitchy Binman.

[b]New Modes[/b]: Classic and Journey have been replaced with Classic and Extended. These now refer to two new ways of playing the game.

[i]Classic[/i]: The concise, focused journey. Features minor gameplay elements. Around 60 minutes in length.

[i]Extended[/i]: Features additional gameplay and 3 extra chapters. Around 90 minutes in length.

Extended is the original and what you’ve all been playing. I implemented the shorter Classic Mode as I believe it plays better in one sitting with some of the fat trimmed. Classic omits The Ravine, Half of The Causeway and The Canyon.

[b]New Sound[/b]: The Adjudicator, Binman and The Wanderer all have new sound. The chapters The Cathedral, The Overpass and The Reprimand all have rehauled environment sound. An easter egg in The Run now has its own hum.

[b]Tutorial[/b]: The Leap tutorial at The Door is more comprehensive and easier to understand. Animations will now also appear to indicate how grabbing works if players are stuck and indicators for leaping now appear if players take too long in case they haven’t got to grips with it.

[b]Snap Turn/Smooth Turn[/b]: Toggle has been moved to the Main Menu/Pause Menu.



[u][b]Other Changes[/b][/u]

[b]Menus[/b]

[list]
[*] The Kinglumps intro has been changed and now features the Biennale logo for this year's film festival.
[*] The menu has been improved. The sculpture park has been moved to Chapter select.
[*] Continue and Main Menu have been swapped in the pause menu.
[*] You can no longer teleport in the Main Menu area.
[/list]
[b]Chapters[/b]

[i][u]The View/View Ravine[/u][/i]

[list]
[*] The View’s first two cave chambers have been removed.
[*] Classic mode now features an alternative Ravine (head fly-by section) that leads into The Cathedral.
[/list]
[i][u]The Cathedral[/u][/i]

[list]
[*] The Cathedral now has an environment/ambient loop.
[*] The Primordial watchers now have sound in The Cathedral.
[*] All leaps except the final one have been removed as I felt they were unnecessary.
[/list]
[i][u]The Computer[/u][/i]

[list]
[*] Only extended mode requires you to jump from the Cable avoiding the aggressive slug. Classic lets you teleport.
[*] The Final leap has been changed to make it easier. This leap was far too hard.
[/list]
[i][u]The Maze[/u][/i]

[list]
[*] The Maze now appears with a hint if you die more than 5 times.
[/list]
[i][u]The Graveyard[/u][/i]

No Changes
[i][u]The Run[/u][/i]

[list]
[*] The music has been fixed so the transitions are smooth and loops no longer pop.
[*] The Easter egg known as “The Human” now has sound.
[/list]
[i][u]The Bowl[/u][/i]

No Changes

[i][u]The Boulder[/u][/i]

[list]
[*] The Death respawn for the leap is no more forgiving.
[*] The Fog transition to The Causeway is cleaner.
[/list]
[i][u]The Causeway[/u][/i]

[list]
[*] There are now two versions of the Causeway. Long and Short. Long is the original and reserved for classic mode. Short has the cave about midway through.
[*] The Boulder Smash Event triggers earlier.
[*] Some of the pillars move in a more forgiving way.
[*] The Wanderer vista sequence triggers earlier.
[*] Some of the Jumpers don’t throw you as high into the sky.
[/list]
[i][u]The Overpass[/u][/i]

[list]
[*] Overhauled sound for the main cave chamber and new sound for the Wanderer.
[*] The leap has been removed as it was too small to merit something more than a teleport.
[*] Teleporting outside of the map at the beginning has been fixed.
[/list]
[i][u]The Adjudicator[/u][/i]

[list]

[/list]
[i][u]The Forest[/u][/i]

[list]
[*] The Predator coming straight towards you at the end and killing you is less of a death sentence. You can now see him coming earlier and avoid him.
[*] You are no longer required to leap at the end before grabbing the orb but it may still help to do so.
[*] The Predator will surprise you if you’re dumb enough to try and go into the cave he comes out of after his first appearance.
[/list]
[i][u]The Canyon[/u][/i]

[list]
[*] The Canyon only appears in Extended mode.
[/list]
[i][u]The Mouth[/u][/i]

[list]
[*] Two versions of The Mouth exist now. One now has the chamber cave from the beginning of The Canyon should the player play Classic Mode.
[*] Bin Man is much bigger and blocks out the ‘sun’ for longer.
[/list]
[u][i]The Pendulum[/i][/u]

No Changes

[i][u]The Bottom[/u][/i]

[list]

[/list]
[i][u]The Meeting[/u][/i]

No Changes

[/list]

[/list]

notes.title: Audio Overhaul Part 1
notes.content:
[u][b]Main Changes[/b][/u]

[b]WEAR HEADPHONES WEAR HEADPHONES WEAR HEADPHONES[/b]

- The audio for the game has been rebuilt using Oculus Audio for better spatalization which is much more immersive.
- The entire game has a new mix. Oculus Quest should be much louder and headphone users have much more range.
- All Music sits higher in the mix which improves the game tenfold.
- Some new and improved sound has been added to some of the chapters.
- All chapters have had a pass on sound so environment sound/ambience/SFX are mixed much better. 
- The wind is windier.

[i]NOTE: If you are using a Quest 2 like me without headphones then there is no hope for you. This update has improved things but please wear headphones if you don't want low end snap, crackle and pop. The game has a lot of low-end sounds which suck on Quest because the ZUCK probably thought people would only play laser quest or San Francisco hiking games. Blessed are Index users.[/i]

Other Changes

- The Forest entrance has been redecorated with rocks.
- The Canyon vista has been improved again. You can now see the causeway and the adjudicator if you squint.
- Bin Man eye's have a new super freaky deaky wacky crackle sound.
- The Adjudicators in the Reprimand turn much quicker.
- Bin Man pervs on you from further away in the Toilet section making him strangely more sinister. 
- Faster Smooth turn options
- Lots of stuff I didn't write down.


[b]Part 1 of the Audio overhaul is a New Mix. Part 2 will be more focused on Sound Design. [/b]

notes.title: Update - Texture Optimization and Anti Aliasing Options

[b]Note[/b]: Some people have been running into an issue where they see a cubey noisy mess in one eye, mainly in The Forest chapter. I've rebuilt the lighting for that level so anyone who has had that issue please tell me if it persists. If it remains try turning the anti-aliasing off to see if that fixes it. Apologies for the issue, with all Bs like this its hard to know if its something I can fix or whether its an Unreal Engine/HMD issue.

Other

Lots of minor changes that I forgot to write down.

notes.title: Minor Update following Update V1.1
notes.content:
Main Changes

- The text in the intro has more information regarding your journey. (I don't think I gave you folks enough to understand what the f*** was going on. Things make a marginal amount more sense now). The text now reads:

"At the edge of the Universe lies The Utility Room.
The behind the scenes where all the heavy lifting takes place.
Beyond its doors, a Supreme Being known only as Bin Man or 'The Cosmic Caretaker'
oversees the work required to keep existence stable and temporal.
(Fade text, Fade in)
There have been no work incidents in 13.8 Billion years
You are arriving as a tourist. Don't do anything Foolish."

The world of The Utility Room makes sense to me, and revealing too much I feel is detriment to its effectiveness as a piece of work. It should speak for itself, but I do think the context this gives enriches the world and contextualises the madness and confusion at the end of the journey. Please disagree :)

- The 'glitching' effect on the text has also been removed. I thought it was corny.

- I have remade the animation in the first Ravine that I refer to as the fly-by. Some of you have referred to this as "the ghost" or "the weird white thing" because it happens too quickly. This was intended to be a minor jumpscare of a Worker head (The small heads that zoom around and stare at you). I've made the fly-by more dynamic so its easier to take in.

- I've added some minor stars facing away from the entrance to The Utility Room. I do not know if you would be able to see any stars from the edge of the Universe but I've added them in anyway. If a science man could clarify that'd be ace.

- I've fixed the fall-reset If you miss the first jump at The Door. I discovered that if you are clenching the grip as you fall it wouldn't reset you. This was gamebreaking. Thanks to @BiscuitOne for discovering this.

- The load screen has been reduced by 2 seconds and the font has been changed.

notes.title: Added Jump / Bug fixes and other changes
notes.content:
Main Updates

- Added Jump
- Renamed the original jump/haptic jump to 'leap'. Jump can be used for small gaps but leap is needed for big gaps.
- You can now change direction whilst in the air.
- Redesigned The Computer jump puzzle to accomodate the new jump - makes it less punishing and more like a traditional platformer.
- Redesigned the Cathedral so that the entire level can be played without Teleport if the player chooses to use jump and leap.
- rewrote the jump tutorial - "Some gaps are to big to be jumped. They must be leaped.
- Adjusted the teleport blocking volumes so that they cant be 'cheesed' with a jump and teleport.
- Binman's Car Park is now black and white.
- Added a jump to Journey mode that is used to get on the head during The Maze
- Optimized The Sculpture Park




Various changes and bug fixes

Replaced most of the textures in the game with virtual textures. This should give a performance boost with the tradeoff being some noise in distant textures
Increased the speed of the Wanderer in The Causeway level.
Made the Watcher texture in The Run the standard for all levels.
Increased the distance the player must first jump at The Door
Increased the ceiling height in the first cave so the player doesnt collide and fall to their death.
relit the Worker flyby in the ravine immediately after The View so it doesn't look like a ghost.
Moved the pillars around on the Ravine so you can jump between them.
Removed one of the leaps from the end of The Cathedral
Fixed the teleport glitch when you arrive at The Door that lasted for 4 seconds.
Relit the Graveyard
Relit the first cave in The Overpass
Decreased the tiling size on The Finale so the texture moving across the landscape is more obvious

notes.content:
- Remove foveated rendering. It improved performance but caused a massive artifact glitch on one of the eyes on some peoples headsets. Hopefully Unreal Engine will fix it in the future as this issue has been around for a year now. Seems to happen less often but its nonetheless broken.

- Added a smooth turn setting. Speeds 1 - 5. Available on the Pause menu

notes.title: Performance Boost - Optimized textures and Fixed Foveated Rendering
notes.content:
- Optimized some textures using Virtual Textures
- Added Fixed Foveated Rendering which should generate a decent performance boost.
- Removed some of the dynamic shadows on the Workers during The Bottom which should improve performance also.

notes.title: Movement Overhaul - Classic Mode
notes.content: - Smooth Locomotion and Teleport have been combined to make a single mode called "Classic Mode". This allows players to use whatever they want, whenever they want. The left thumbstick controls smooth locomotion and the right thumbstick controls Teleport and Turn. THere are now only two modes in the game. Classic and Journey. Journey is teleport only and increases the teleport distance and is inteded for a relaxed playthrough of the game. Hopefully this resolves a lot of the issues and confusion surrounding movement modes and meets everybodys preference. Have Fun!
